summary: Willamette NF cabin on Scott Mountain, Lane County: built 1929, removed or burned by 1960; sources disagree on the year and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Cathedral cabin per the register and firelookout.com; a June 1929 Eugene paper had called the planned building a fire chaser house of the tower variety
facts.status_note: Removed in 1959 or 1960 per the Rex page and register, or destroyed in 1960 per firelookout.com; a group found it burned in August 1960

events.note: Cabin built on the summit. Newspapers in June to August 1929 describe pack-mule supply and near completion by late August
Rex page entry dated 1959; the register says removed in 1960 and firelookout.com says destroyed in 1960
A hiking group reached the lookout in August 1960 and found it had burned
Date registered May 13, 2011 per the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A June 1929 Eugene Register item called the planned building a fire chaser house of the tower variety. The register and firelookout.com call the built structure a cathedral cabin. The story reports both terms.

The Rex page has a 1959 removal entry, the register says removed in 1960, and firelookout.com says destroyed in 1960. A group found it burned in August 1960. The story gives the spread and does not pick one year.

notes_for_editor: No source describes what remains on the site today, and access is unknown. Removal year conflicts (1959 Rex, 1960 register and firelookout.com). A search snippet calls the peak part of the Mount Washington Wilderness, but the page fetched empty, so it is not cited; check wilderness status before any access sentence. The register shows a 1955 photo credited to Ed Anderson, but no image URL was captured, so no photo is listed. The 1928 newspaper note about a telephone line and secondary lookout point is left out because it does not describe the cabin.
